methodologySummary: RateReveal admits a merchant-facing effective-rate range only when concrete, individually identified source documents and their quantitative inputs can be traced directly and both displayed boundaries reconstruct under a reviewed derivation. The prior restaurant and grocery ranges remain directionally plausible but are unavailable because the legacy source list does not reproduce either exact all-in range.

provenanceReview.conclusion: No reviewed material supplies a reproducible derivation from concrete source observations to either exact all-in effective-rate range. Network schedules establish transaction-level interchange inputs, not a merchant all-in range; the traceable industry article is explicitly rough and general; and the legacy internal claims do not include a pinned cohort artifact or boundary calculation. Both candidates therefore fail merchant-display admission.

sourceAssessments.title: Visa USA Interchange Reimbursement Fees
sourceAssessments.locationWithinSource: Introduction and category/card-product interchange tables, including restaurant and supermarket programs
sourceAssessments.finding: This is a concrete primary schedule for Visa interchange reimbursement fees. Visa distinguishes interchange from the merchant discount and the document does not supply an all-in effective-rate distribution, processor markup, merchant card mix, or a derivation to either candidate range.

sourceAssessments.title: Mastercard 2025–2026 U.S. Region Interchange Programs and Rates
sourceAssessments.locationWithinSource: Consumer credit tables containing restaurant and supermarket interchange programs
sourceAssessments.finding: This is a concrete primary schedule for Mastercard interchange programs. It provides transaction-level category and card-product costs but not an all-in merchant effective-rate distribution, processor markup, card-mix model, or a derivation to either candidate range. The publication date is represented only by the document copyright year, another limitation for admission.

sourceAssessments.title: Average Credit Card Processing Fees — How Much Does It Cost?
sourceAssessments.locationWithinSource: Average Credit Card Processing Fees and Effective Rate sections
sourceAssessments.finding: The article gives rough general card-present and card-not-present cost context and warns that averages vary with processing method, ticket size, debit mix, and other fees. It is not category-and-volume-specific evidence for either exact restaurant or grocery range and has no stable publication/effective date in the reviewed page metadata.

sourceAssessments.title: Legacy benchmark source-list claims
sourceAssessments.finding: The legacy list names MerchantCostConsulting, Swipesum, Corepay, and CardFellow without individual document titles, direct locators, publication/effective dates, per-entry linkage, or extracted quantitative observations. It is an internal pointer to unverified claims rather than independently traceable source provenance.

sourceAssessments.title: Legacy real-statement cross-check claim
sourceAssessments.finding: The legacy file states that named Fiserv statements were used for cross-verification but provides no pinned anonymized cohort artifact, inclusion criteria, observed effective rates, category/account-coding verification, statistical method, or calculation that reproduces the candidate boundaries. It can support directional plausibility only.

candidateRangeAssessments.derivationFinding: No source or reproducible combination of source observations establishes 2.10% as the lower boundary and 2.60% as the upper boundary for U.S. standard-risk card-present Fiserv restaurant merchants in the $100,000–$500,000 annual-volume tier. The legacy range is asserted rather than derived.
evidenceGaps: A pinned, category-verified observation set or explicit card-mix, ticket-size, assessment, and processor-markup model is absent.
There is no machine-reconstructable calculation linking individually located source metrics to both exact range boundaries.
The legacy real-statement check has no reproducible anonymized cohort artifact or selection methodology.

The legacy range is asserted rather than derived.
